Lemma
[a geodesic satisfies the geodesic equation at the initial time]

↗ def:dc-ch3-2-1 ↗ lem:dc-ch3-2-5-exist ↗ lem:dc-ch3-2-5-velocity

1. ch3:2.5A geodesic with initial data $(p,v)$ — the base projection of an integral curve of the geodesic field — satisfies the second-order geodesic equation of section 1 at the initial time: in the chart at the foot $\gamma (0)=p$, the chart curve $x=\varphi _p\circ \gamma $ has a second derivative at $0$ and $x''(0)+\Gamma _p(v,v)(x(0))=0$. The same holds for the canonical maximal geodesic. This bridges the first-order (geodesic-field) formulation back to the second-order equation at the initial time.
Proof

\sketch

With $(x,w)$ as in subsection 1.1, the first-order system gives $x'=w$ near $0$ and $w'(0)=-\Gamma _p(w(0),w(0))(x(0))$; hence $x'$ is differentiable at $0$ with $x''(0)=w'(0)=-\Gamma _p(v,v)(x(0))$, which is the geodesic equation at $0$.

□
